stem: Log files in S3 are read often for 30 days, rarely for the next 60 days, and must then be kept for 7 years but are almost never read. Which lifecycle plan costs least?
options: Move logs to S3 One Zone-IA on day one and leave them there for good
Intelligent-Tiering from day one with no archive tiers turned on
Keep all logs in S3 Standard for the whole seven years of retention
Standard, then Standard-IA at 30 days, then Glacier Deep Archive at 90 days
explanation: Lifecycle transitions match storage cost to access: Standard while hot, Standard-IA (30-day minimum) for rare access, and Deep Archive, the cheapest class, for long retention with retrieval in hours. Without archive tiers, Intelligent-Tiering would not reach Deep Archive prices.

stem: An order website sends orders straight to a processing tier. During sales the processing tier falls behind and orders are lost. Which change makes the system resilient to these spikes?
options: Put an Amazon SQS queue between the web tier and the processing tier
Move the processing tier to one larger EC2 instance with more memory
Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the processing tier
Replace the processing tier's EBS volumes with Provisioned IOPS volumes
explanation: An SQS queue buffers orders durably so the web tier can accept them at any rate and the processors work through the backlog at their own pace. A larger single instance still has a ceiling and is a single point of failure.

stem: A company's Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database must keep running with automatic failover if an Availability Zone fails, without any application change. What should the architect enable?
options: A larger DB instance class
Automated backups every hour
A read replica in the same AZ
A Multi-AZ deployment
explanation: Multi-AZ keeps a synchronous standby in another AZ and fails over automatically, and the DNS endpoint stays the same. Backups restore data but do not provide automatic failover.

stem: A database on EC2 needs 40,000 IOPS with consistent sub-millisecond latency and 99.999% volume durability. Which EBS volume type fits?
options: Throughput Optimized HDD (st1)
General Purpose SSD (gp3) at its baseline
Cold HDD (sc1)
Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2 Block Express)
explanation: io2 Block Express is built for I/O-heavy databases, with provisioned IOPS up to 256,000, sub-millisecond latency and 99.999% durability. gp3 starts at a 3,000 IOPS baseline and is designed for 99.8 to 99.9% durability. HDD volumes are for throughput, not IOPS.

stem: A product catalog on Amazon RDS gets the same read queries thousands of times per second, and the database CPU is maxed out. Which change cuts database load the most?
options: Move the RDS storage to Provisioned IOPS
Cache query results in Amazon ElastiCache
Turn on Multi-AZ for the RDS instance
Take automated snapshots every five minutes
explanation: An in-memory cache serves repeated reads in microseconds to milliseconds and keeps them away from the database. Multi-AZ adds a standby that does not serve reads, and storage IOPS do not fix CPU spent on repeated queries.

stem: An application on Amazon EC2 instances must read objects from an Amazon S3 bucket. The security team forbids long-term credentials stored on the instances. What should a solutions architect do?
options: Create an IAM user and store its access keys in the application config
Make the bucket public and restrict it with a referer condition
Attach an IAM role to the instances through an instance profile
Store an IAM user's access keys in an encrypted file on the EBS volume
explanation: An instance profile gives the instance an IAM role, and the instance metadata service hands the application temporary credentials that rotate automatically. Access keys for an IAM user are long-term credentials whether or not the file holding them is encrypted.

stem: A three-tier web application runs web servers behind an Application Load Balancer and a MySQL database on Amazon RDS. The database must not be reachable from the internet. Where should the RDS instance go?
options: In public subnets, with a network ACL that blocks all inbound traffic
In public subnets, with a security group that allows 0.0.0.0/0 on port 3306
In private subnets, with a security group that allows the web tier's group
In the same subnet as the load balancer, with a public IP address
explanation: Private subnets have no route to an internet gateway, and a security group that references the web tier's security group lets only those instances connect on 3306. A public subnet with a blanket NACL deny would also block the web tier.

stem: An Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance was created without encryption. Compliance now requires encryption at rest. What should the solutions architect do?
options: Modify the DB instance and select the encryption option in the console
Snapshot it, copy the snapshot with encryption, and restore from the copy
Add an SSL certificate to the instance and require TLS for all clients
Turn on EBS encryption by default in the Region and reboot the instance
explanation: Encryption for an RDS instance can only be chosen at creation. The supported path is to copy an unencrypted snapshot with encryption enabled and restore a new encrypted instance from it. TLS protects data in transit, not at rest.

stem: A data lake holds objects whose access patterns are unknown and change over time. Some objects are hot for a week then cold for months. The team wants savings without retrieval fees or lifecycle tuning. Which storage class fits?
options: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
S3 Intelligent-Tiering
S3 One Zone-IA
S3 Standard-IA
explanation: Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between access tiers automatically based on use, for a small monitoring charge per object and no retrieval fees. Standard-IA charges retrieval fees, which hurt when cold objects turn hot again.

stem: When an order is placed, three independent services (billing, shipping and analytics) must each receive a copy of the event and process it at their own pace. Which design fits?
options: Have the web tier call each service's API one after another in a loop
Write each order to an S3 bucket and have every service list the bucket
Publish to an SNS topic with an SQS queue subscribed for each service
Send each order to a single SQS queue that all three services poll
explanation: SNS to SQS fan-out delivers a copy of each message to every subscribed queue, and each queue buffers for its own consumer. With one shared queue each message goes to only one consumer.

stem: A web application runs on six EC2 instances in one Availability Zone behind an ALB. What change best improves availability?
options: Run the Auto Scaling group across at least two AZs
Attach an Elastic IP address to each instance
Double the instance size and keep the single AZ
Move all six instances to a cluster placement group
explanation: An Auto Scaling group spanning multiple AZs, with the ALB enabled in those AZs, keeps serving if one AZ fails and replaces unhealthy instances. A cluster placement group concentrates instances even more tightly.

stem: A log processing cluster reads large files sequentially and needs high throughput at the lowest cost per GB. Data is accessed often. Which EBS volume type fits?
options: Cold HDD (sc1)
General Purpose SSD (gp3)
Throughput Optimized HDD (st1)
Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2 Block Express)
explanation: st1 is low-cost HDD storage designed for frequently accessed, throughput-heavy sequential workloads such as big data and log processing. sc1 is cheaper but meant for infrequently accessed data, and SSD types cost more per GB.

stem: A gaming leaderboard on DynamoDB needs read latency in microseconds for hot items, with no changes to the application's data access logic beyond the client. Which service fits?
options: DynamoDB global tables
Amazon CloudFront caching
DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)
Amazon RDS cross-Region read replicas
explanation: DAX is an in-memory cache built for DynamoDB that is API-compatible, so applications switch to the DAX client and get microsecond reads. Global tables replicate across Regions but still read at single-digit milliseconds.

stem: A company runs a steady fleet of EC2 instances 24/7 and expects to move between instance families and Regions, and to adopt Fargate and Lambda, over the next three years. Which purchase option saves the most while keeping that flexibility?
options: EC2 Instance Savings Plans
Compute Savings Plans
Standard Reserved Instances
Spot Instances for the base load
explanation: Compute Savings Plans apply a committed hourly spend to EC2 in any family, size or Region, and to Fargate and Lambda. EC2 Instance Savings Plans and Standard RIs give deeper discounts but lock in an instance family in a Region.

stem: A company with 40 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations wants employees to sign in once with their corporate identity provider and reach only the accounts and permissions assigned to their job. Which solution needs the least ongoing effort?
options: Amazon Cognito user pools linked to each account's IAM users
An IAM user per employee in every account, grouped by job role
IAM Identity Center with permission sets assigned to groups
One shared IAM user per team with credentials kept in a vault
explanation: IAM Identity Center federates with the corporate identity provider and pushes permission sets into each assigned account as roles, so access is managed in one place. Per-account IAM users multiply credentials, and Cognito is for application users, not workforce access to AWS accounts.

stem: A company must block all traffic from one known malicious IP address to every instance in a subnet. Security groups are already in use. What should be added?
options: A deny rule for that address in the subnet's network ACL
An AWS Shield Standard subscription for the affected VPC
A deny rule for that address in each instance's security group
A route table entry that sends the address to a NAT gateway
explanation: Network ACLs support explicit deny rules at the subnet level. Security groups only have allow rules, so they cannot deny one address while allowing everyone else.

stem: A financial firm must keep trade records in Amazon S3 for seven years so that no user, including the root user, can delete or overwrite them during that time. What should be configured?
options: A bucket policy that denies s3:DeleteObject to all IAM users in the account
S3 Object Lock in governance mode with a seven-year retention period
S3 Versioning with a lifecycle rule that expires objects after seven years
S3 Object Lock in compliance mode with a seven-year retention period
explanation: Compliance mode prevents any user, including root, from deleting or overwriting a locked object version until the retention period ends. Governance mode can be bypassed by users with special permission, and a bucket policy can be changed by an administrator.

stem: A nightly batch job processes images, can be stopped and resumed at any time, and has no deadline within the night. Which EC2 purchase option is cheapest?
options: On-Demand Capacity Reservations
Spot Instances
Dedicated Instances
On-Demand Instances
explanation: Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity at up to 90 percent off On-Demand, and AWS can reclaim them with a two-minute warning, which is fine for interruptible, checkpointed work. Capacity Reservations cost the On-Demand price whether used or not.

stem: A banking application must process account transactions exactly once and in the order they were sent for each account. Which service configuration meets this?
options: An SQS FIFO queue using the account ID as the message group ID
An SQS standard queue with a dead-letter queue for failed messages
An SQS standard queue with long polling turned on for the consumers
An SNS standard topic with an email subscription for each account
explanation: FIFO queues preserve order within a message group and deduplicate messages for exactly-once processing. Using the account ID as the group keeps each account in order while different accounts process in parallel. Standard queues offer best-effort ordering and at-least-once delivery.

stem: A company needs a disaster recovery plan for a critical application with an RTO of a few minutes. A scaled-down but fully functional copy should always run in a second Region and scale up on failover. Which strategy is this?
options: Pilot light
Backup and restore
Warm standby
Cold site with tape
explanation: Warm standby keeps a scaled-down, always-running copy of the full stack that can take traffic immediately and scale up. Pilot light keeps only core pieces such as replicated data running, with servers off, so recovery takes longer.

stem: A genomics company runs a compute cluster that needs a file system with hundreds of GB/s of throughput and sub-millisecond latency, reading input data that lives in an S3 bucket. Which service fits?
options: AWS Storage Gateway S3 File Gateway on EC2
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server with SMB
Amazon EFS using the One Zone storage class
Amazon FSx for Lustre linked to S3
explanation: FSx for Lustre is a high-performance parallel file system for HPC and machine learning, and it can link to an S3 bucket to present objects as files and write results back. EFS is general-purpose NFS without Lustre's scale-out throughput.

stem: A media company serves video files and images from S3 to viewers worldwide. Viewers far from the bucket's Region see slow load times. What should the architect add?
options: S3 Cross-Region Replication into one other AWS Region
A Network Load Balancer in front of the S3 bucket
A CloudFront distribution with the S3 origin
Larger EC2 instances in the same Region as the bucket
explanation: CloudFront caches content at edge locations close to viewers, which cuts latency and offloads the origin. Replicating to one more Region helps only viewers near that Region.

stem: Private instances transfer hundreds of TB a month to Amazon S3 in the same Region through a NAT gateway, and NAT gateway charges are high. Which change cuts this cost?
options: Add a gateway VPC endpoint for S3
Add a second NAT gateway in another AZ
Turn on S3 Transfer Acceleration
Move the instances into a public subnet
explanation: Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB have no charge, and traffic through them skips the NAT gateway's per-GB processing fee. Public instances would expose the workload, and Transfer Acceleration adds cost.

stem: A company must ensure that no one in its development accounts, including account administrators, can launch resources outside the us-east-1 and us-west-2 Regions. What should the solutions architect use?
options: An IAM group policy that allows only the two approved Regions
An SCP that denies actions when aws:RequestedRegion is any other Region
AWS Config rules that delete resources found in other Regions
An IAM permissions boundary attached to every administrator in the accounts
explanation: A service control policy in AWS Organizations caps what every principal in the member accounts can do, administrators and the root user included, so a Region deny applies to all. Permissions boundaries can be removed by an administrator with IAM rights, and Config only reacts after the resource exists.

stem: EC2 workers in an Auto Scaling group process messages from an SQS queue. The company wants the group to scale with the amount of work waiting. Which metric should drive scaling?
options: Backlog per instance: visible messages divided by running instances
The SQS queue's NumberOfMessagesDeleted metric averaged over a day
Average CPU utilization of the EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group
Number of HTTP requests that reach the application's load balancer
explanation: AWS recommends target tracking on backlog per instance (ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible divided by the group's running capacity) so capacity follows the queue. CPU may stay low while messages pile up, and there is no load balancer in this design.

stem: A public website behind an Application Load Balancer is receiving SQL injection attempts and bursts of requests from a few IP addresses. Which service mitigates both with managed rules and rate limits?
options: AWS WAF associated with the Application Load Balancer
Amazon Inspector scanning the instances behind the ALB
AWS Shield Standard enabled on the Application Load Balancer
Amazon GuardDuty with automatic remediation turned on
explanation: AWS WAF inspects HTTP requests at the ALB, CloudFront or API Gateway, with managed rule groups for SQL injection and rate-based rules that block noisy IPs. GuardDuty detects threats but does not filter requests, and Shield Standard covers network and transport layer DDoS.

stem: A company wants to encrypt S3 objects with keys it controls, with key usage logged in AWS CloudTrail and the ability to disable a key immediately. Which option fits?
options: SSE-KMS with a customer managed key
SSE-C with keys stored in the bucket next to the data
Client-side encryption with a key kept in the code
SSE-S3 with Amazon S3 managed keys
explanation: With a customer managed KMS key the company controls the key policy, can disable or schedule deletion of the key, and every use is logged in CloudTrail. SSE-S3 keys are fully managed by S3 with no per-key control.

stem: A company suspects many EC2 instances are oversized. Which service analyzes utilization metrics and recommends better instance types and sizes?
options: AWS Budgets alerts
AWS Cost and Usage Report
Amazon Inspector
AWS Compute Optimizer
explanation: Compute Optimizer uses machine learning on CloudWatch metrics to recommend instance types and sizes for EC2, Auto Scaling groups, EBS, Lambda, ECS on Fargate and RDS. Budgets alerts on spend but gives no sizing advice.

stem: A company runs its application in two Regions in an active-passive setup. Traffic should go to the secondary Region automatically if the primary's health check fails. Which Route 53 configuration does this?
options: Weighted routing with equal weights for the two Regions
Simple routing with both Regions' IP addresses in one record
Geolocation routing with a default record for the primary
Failover routing records with health checks on the primary
explanation: Failover routing answers with the primary record while its health check passes and switches to the secondary when it fails. Weighted routing at 50/50 would send traffic to both Regions all the time.

stem: A batch job does heavy mathematical modeling, is limited by CPU, and needs little memory. Which EC2 instance family fits best?
options: Memory optimized (R family)
Compute optimized (C family)
Burstable general purpose (T family)
Storage optimized (I family)
explanation: C family instances have a high ratio of vCPU to memory for compute-bound work such as modeling, batch processing and media encoding. Burstable T instances cannot sustain high CPU without extra charges or throttling.

stem: A company transfers several terabytes a day between its data center and AWS and needs consistent network performance with dedicated bandwidth, not the public internet. Which service fits?
options: S3 Transfer Acceleration
AWS Client VPN
AWS Direct Connect
AWS Site-to-Site VPN
explanation: Direct Connect is a dedicated private connection from the data center to AWS with consistent bandwidth and latency. Site-to-Site VPN is encrypted but travels over the internet, so its performance varies.

stem: An auditing team in Account A needs read-only access to resources in Account B. The company does not want to create IAM users in Account B. What is the most secure approach?
options: Add the auditors' IAM users from Account A to a group in Account B
Create a role in Account B that trusts Account A and let auditors assume it
Copy Account B's resources to Account A on a nightly schedule
Create one IAM user in Account B and share its password with the auditors
explanation: A role in Account B with a trust policy naming Account A lets auditors use AWS STS to get temporary credentials there, with read-only permissions attached to the role. IAM groups can only contain users from their own account, and a shared password removes individual accountability.

stem: A web application stores user session data in memory on each EC2 instance. Users are logged out when Auto Scaling removes an instance. How should the architect fix this so the tier can scale freely?
options: Enable sticky sessions and stop all scale-in events
Store sessions on each instance's root EBS volume
Use larger instances so fewer of them are needed
Store sessions in Amazon ElastiCache or DynamoDB
explanation: Moving session state to a shared store such as ElastiCache or DynamoDB makes the instances stateless, so any instance can serve any request and scale-in loses nothing. Sticky sessions still lose the session when the instance goes away.

stem: A finance team wants an email when a project's forecast monthly spend is about to exceed 5,000 USD, and wants to stop new resource launches automatically at that point. Which service fits?
options: AWS Pricing Calculator
AWS Cost Explorer saved reports
AWS Trusted Advisor checks
AWS Budgets with budget actions
explanation: AWS Budgets alerts on actual or forecast cost, and budget actions can apply an IAM policy or SCP, or stop instances, when a threshold is crossed. Cost Explorer visualizes spend but sends no alerts or actions.

stem: A global e-commerce application uses Amazon Aurora MySQL. It needs reads with low latency in three Regions and recovery in another Region within about a minute, with an RPO of seconds, if the primary Region fails. What should the architect use?
options: An RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment in each Region
Aurora Replicas spread across the primary Region's AZs
Cross-Region automated snapshot copies every hour
Aurora Global Database with secondary Regions
explanation: Aurora Global Database replicates storage to secondary Regions with typical lag under a second, serves local reads there, and can promote a secondary in about a minute. Hourly snapshots give an RPO of up to an hour.

stem: Users around the world upload files of several GB to one S3 bucket in us-east-1, and uploads from distant countries are slow and sometimes fail. Which combination improves this?
options: S3 Standard-IA with a lifecycle policy
S3 Object Lock with versioning enabled
Transfer Acceleration and multipart upload
S3 Same-Region Replication to a second bucket
explanation: Transfer Acceleration routes uploads through the nearest CloudFront edge location and over the AWS backbone, and multipart upload sends parts in parallel and retries only failed parts. AWS recommends multipart for objects over 100 MB.

stem: Analysts need to run ad hoc SQL queries against CSV and Parquet files in Amazon S3 without loading them into a database or managing servers. Which service fits?
options: Amazon ElastiCache
Amazon Athena
Amazon Neptune
Amazon RDS for MySQL
explanation: Athena runs standard SQL directly on data in S3, is serverless and charges by data scanned. Storing data as compressed, partitioned Parquet cuts the data scanned. RDS would require loading the data first.

stem: A new application's DynamoDB table has unpredictable traffic with long idle periods and sudden spikes. The team wants to pay only for the requests it makes. Which capacity mode fits?
options: Provisioned mode with fixed capacity
Provisioned mode with reserved capacity
Provisioned mode set for the peak load
On-demand capacity mode
explanation: On-demand mode bills per request and scales instantly, which suits unknown or spiky traffic. Reserved capacity is a commitment that only pays off for steady, predictable throughput.

stem: Instances in private subnets call Amazon S3 and AWS Systems Manager. The company wants this traffic to stay off the internet and to remove the NAT gateway. What should the architect add?
options: A VPC peering connection to the AWS Region's public service network
An internet gateway and public IP addresses on every one of the instances
An S3 gateway endpoint and interface endpoints for Systems Manager
An egress-only internet gateway attached to the private subnets
explanation: Gateway endpoints route S3 (and DynamoDB) traffic privately, and interface endpoints powered by AWS PrivateLink give private IPs for services such as Systems Manager. An egress-only internet gateway is for outbound IPv6 and still uses the internet.

stem: A regulation requires that encryption keys live in single-tenant hardware security modules validated at FIPS 140-3 Level 3 that the company alone controls, with AWS having no access to the keys. Which service meets this?
options: AWS KMS with AWS managed keys
AWS CloudHSM
Amazon S3 SSE-S3 encryption
AWS Secrets Manager
explanation: CloudHSM provides dedicated HSMs in the customer's VPC, and the customer manages the users and keys. AWS KMS HSMs are also FIPS validated, but they are multi-tenant and operated by AWS, so KMS does not meet a single-tenant requirement.

stem: A loan approval process has several steps, some run by Lambda functions and one that waits up to five days for a human approval, with retries and error handling between steps. Which service should coordinate it?
options: AWS Lambda with a 15-minute timeout
AWS Step Functions
Amazon EventBridge Scheduler
Amazon SQS standard queue
explanation: Step Functions Standard Workflows run for up to a year, can wait for a callback token from a human task, and define retries and catch blocks for each state. A Lambda invocation stops after 15 minutes.

stem: A new AWS account was just created. Which action best protects the root user?
options: Rename the root user so attackers cannot guess the sign-in name
Share the root password with two administrators for redundancy
Enable MFA on the root user and do not create root access keys
Create root access keys and store them in AWS Secrets Manager
explanation: AWS recommends MFA on the root user, no root access keys, and daily work done with other identities. The root user cannot be renamed, and keeping its access keys anywhere still leaves unrestricted long-term credentials in existence.

stem: A web application serves large downloads directly from EC2 instances to internet users, and data transfer out is the largest line on the bill. Which change typically lowers this cost?
options: Move the instances into a second AWS Region
Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer
Serve the downloads through CloudFront
Attach larger EBS volumes to each instance
explanation: CloudFront caches content at the edge, and data transfer from the origin to CloudFront is free, while CloudFront's own transfer out is usually priced lower than EC2's and cuts origin load. A second Region adds cost.

stem: A VPC has private subnets in three AZs that all route internet traffic through one zonal NAT gateway in AZ A. What is the risk and the fix?
options: The NAT gateway will throttle; replace it with an internet gateway
Traffic is unencrypted; add a VPN connection to the NAT gateway
A zonal NAT gateway fails over to another AZ by itself, so no change is needed
If AZ A fails all subnets lose egress; add a NAT gateway in each AZ
explanation: A zonal NAT gateway is redundant within its own AZ only. AWS recommends one zonal NAT gateway per AZ, with each AZ's route table pointing at its local gateway, so one AZ's failure does not cut egress for the others. (A NAT gateway created in the newer regional availability mode spreads across AZs on its own; a zonal one never does.)

stem: A computational fluid dynamics application runs across many EC2 instances that exchange data constantly and need the lowest possible network latency between nodes. Which configuration fits?
options: A spread placement group across three Availability Zones
A partition placement group with default networking settings
A cluster placement group with Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA)
Instances in different Regions joined by VPC peering links
explanation: A cluster placement group packs instances close together in one AZ for low latency and high throughput, and EFA adds OS-bypass networking for MPI workloads. Spreading across AZs or Regions adds latency.

stem: A company has 60 VPCs in several accounts plus a Direct Connect link to its data center. Production and development VPCs must stay isolated from each other, yet all of them must reach a shared-services VPC and on premises, without a mesh of peering connections. Which service fits?
options: A NAT gateway in each of the VPCs
VPC peering between all pairs of VPCs
VPC gateway endpoints in each VPC
AWS Transit Gateway with separate route tables
explanation: Transit Gateway is a regional hub that VPCs, VPNs and Direct Connect attach to, and separate transit gateway route tables let production and development each reach shared services and on premises but not each other. VPC peering is not transitive, so 60 VPCs would need up to 1,770 connections.

stem: Every image uploaded to an S3 bucket must be resized into a thumbnail within seconds. Uploads range from zero to thousands per minute. Which design scales with the least operational effort?
options: An S3 event notification that invokes a Lambda function
A cron job on an EC2 instance that lists the bucket each hour
An EC2 Auto Scaling group with a fixed size of ten instances
An AWS Batch job queue that is submitted manually every day
explanation: S3 event notifications invoke Lambda for each new object, and Lambda scales with the number of uploads without servers to manage. An hourly cron job misses the within-seconds requirement.

stem: A company is moving SQL Server Enterprise to EC2. Its existing licenses are counted per physical core, and auditors require proof of which physical server each instance ran on over time. Which option meets both needs?
options: EC2 Spot Instances
Compute Savings Plans
EC2 Dedicated Hosts
EC2 Dedicated Instances
explanation: Dedicated Hosts give visibility into the sockets and physical cores of a server dedicated to the customer, which is what per-core licenses require, and host affinity and AWS Config tracking show which host an instance ran on. Dedicated Instances run on single-tenant hardware but do not expose the host's sockets and cores.

stem: An application connects to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database with a password stored in its configuration file. The company needs the password stored securely and rotated automatically every 30 days. What should be used?
options: An encrypted environment variable on the EC2 instance
AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store standard tier
AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation
An Amazon S3 object encrypted with SSE-S3
explanation: Secrets Manager stores credentials encrypted with KMS and has built-in rotation for Amazon RDS databases on a schedule. Parameter Store can hold secure strings but has no native rotation.

stem: A security audit requires that all requests to an S3 bucket use encrypted connections. How can this be enforced?
options: Enable default encryption with SSE-S3 on the bucket and its objects
Deny requests in the bucket policy when aws:SecureTransport is false
Turn on S3 Versioning and MFA Delete for every object in the bucket
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration so traffic uses edge locations instead
explanation: The aws:SecureTransport condition key is false for plain HTTP requests, so a deny statement rejects them. Default encryption protects data at rest, not the connection.

stem: Developers must be allowed to create IAM roles for their Lambda functions, but no role they create may ever have more permissions than a set the security team defines. Which IAM feature enforces this?
options: A trust policy on the developers' role naming the Lambda service
An inline policy on each developer that lists the allowed actions
IAM Access Analyzer policy generation run on a weekly schedule
A permissions boundary required on each new role
explanation: A permissions boundary sets the maximum permissions an identity can have. Requiring it through a condition on iam:CreateRole stops developers from creating roles that exceed it. A trust policy only controls who can assume a role, and Access Analyzer reports on access rather than enforcing a ceiling.

stem: A cost review finds dozens of unattached EBS volumes and idle load balancers left from old projects. Which service highlights such waste with built-in checks?
options: Amazon GuardDuty findings
AWS CloudTrail
AWS Artifact
AWS Trusted Advisor
explanation: Trusted Advisor's cost optimization checks flag idle load balancers, underutilized EC2 instances, unassociated Elastic IPs and other waste (the full set needs Business Support or higher). CloudTrail records API activity, not cost.

stem: Linux EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across three AZs need a shared POSIX file system that survives the loss of an AZ. Which storage fits?
options: An EBS volume with Multi-Attach shared by all instances
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server, Single-AZ deployment
Instance store volumes replicated by a nightly cron job
Amazon EFS with the Regional (Standard) storage class
explanation: EFS Regional file systems store data redundantly across multiple AZs and can be mounted at the same time by instances in every AZ. EBS volumes, Multi-Attach included, live in one AZ.

stem: A Lambda function that processes images is CPU-bound and runs slowly. How can the architect give it more CPU?
options: Add reserved concurrency to the function
Raise the function's timeout setting
Raise the function's memory setting
Move the function into a private subnet
explanation: Lambda allocates CPU in proportion to configured memory (up to 10,240 MB, about 6 vCPUs), so more memory also means more CPU. The timeout only allows longer runs, it does not make them faster.

stem: A company wants to discover the schema of new datasets in S3, keep a central metadata catalog, and run serverless ETL jobs to convert them to Parquet. Which service fits?
options: AWS DataSync
Amazon EMR on EC2
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
AWS Glue
explanation: AWS Glue crawlers infer schemas into the Glue Data Catalog, and Glue ETL jobs run serverless Spark to transform data. EMR can do the transformation but means managing clusters.

stem: A company has many SaaS and AWS event sources and wants to route events to different targets based on content, such as sending only orders over a certain amount to a fraud-check Lambda function. Which service fits best?
options: AWS Step Functions Express Workflows polling each event source
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with a single shard for all events
Amazon SQS FIFO queues, one for each kind of event that arrives
Amazon EventBridge with rules that match on event patterns
explanation: EventBridge rules match events by content (including numeric ranges) and route them to targets, and EventBridge has built-in integrations with SaaS partners. SNS can also filter on message attributes, but EventBridge is the event bus built for many sources and content routing.

stem: Developers' EC2 instances and RDS databases run 24/7 but are used only 9 AM to 6 PM on weekdays. What is the simplest way to cut their cost?
options: Move the instances to Dedicated Hosts in one AZ
Stop the resources outside working hours on a schedule
Turn on detailed monitoring for every instance
Buy three-year Reserved Instances for every resource
explanation: Stopping the instances and databases nights and weekends (for example with AWS Instance Scheduler or EventBridge Scheduler) removes about 70 percent of their compute hours. Reserved Instances pay for 24/7 usage that is not needed.

stem: A security team wants continuous detection of compromised EC2 instances and unusual API calls, plus automated scanning of instances and container images for software vulnerabilities. Which services meet these needs? (Choose two.)
options: Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Artifact
AWS Trusted Advisor
Amazon Macie
Amazon Inspector
explanation: GuardDuty analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs to detect threats such as crypto-mining or credential misuse. Inspector scans EC2 instances, ECR images and Lambda functions for known CVEs. Macie finds sensitive data in S3, and Artifact provides compliance reports.

stem: A company wants to recover quickly if an employee accidentally deletes or overwrites objects in a critical S3 bucket. Which features help? (Choose two.)
options: Enable server access logging and keep the logs in a second bucket
Use the S3 One Zone-IA storage class
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration
Require MFA Delete for permanently deleting versions
Enable S3 Versioning on the bucket
explanation: Versioning keeps prior versions so an overwrite or delete can be undone, and MFA Delete requires MFA to permanently delete a version or change versioning state. Access logs record what happened but do not restore anything.

stem: A company wants to find and remove permissions that are broader than its IAM roles actually need, and to detect any S3 bucket shared with an external account. Which steps help? (Choose two.)
options: Replace every IAM role with IAM users that have long-term access keys
Use IAM Access Analyzer to find resources shared outside the organization
Turn on S3 Transfer Acceleration for the buckets that hold shared data
Review IAM last-accessed data and generate policies from CloudTrail activity
Attach the AdministratorAccess policy to every role so that nothing fails unexpectedly
explanation: Last-accessed information and Access Analyzer policy generation (based on CloudTrail logs) show which permissions a role really uses, and Access Analyzer's external access findings flag buckets, keys and roles shared outside the zone of trust. Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads and has nothing to do with access.

stem: A company must back up EC2, EBS, RDS and DynamoDB resources on a schedule from one place, and keep copies in a second Region for disaster recovery. Which steps meet this? (Choose two.)
options: Write a cron job on each instance that copies files to S3
Create AWS Backup plans that target resources by tag
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the backup bucket
Add a cross-Region copy rule to the backup plan
Turn on Multi-AZ for every RDS database as the backup
explanation: AWS Backup centrally schedules backups across many services, selecting resources by tag, and a copy rule sends recovery points to a vault in another Region. Multi-AZ improves availability but is not a backup: a deleted table is deleted on the standby too.

stem: An application on EC2 needs very fast scratch space for temporary files that can be lost without harm, and its database volume must keep data if the instance stops. Which choices fit? (Choose two.)
options: An EBS volume for the database data
Instance store volumes for the database data
Instance store volumes for the scratch files
Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval for scratch
Amazon EFS One Zone-IA for the database data
explanation: Instance store is physically attached NVMe storage with very high I/O, but its data is lost when the instance stops or terminates, which is fine for scratch. EBS persists independently of the instance, which suits the database.

stem: Match the need to the purpose-built database. Which pairings are correct? (Choose two.)
options: Petabyte-scale analytic SQL warehouse: Amazon Redshift
Fraud graph of linked accounts: Amazon Neptune
Ad hoc SQL over S3 files: Amazon Neptune
Key-value shopping cart data at any scale: Amazon Redshift
Microsecond cache layer: Amazon Aurora
explanation: Neptune is a graph database for highly connected data such as fraud rings and social networks, and Redshift is a columnar data warehouse for analytics. Key-value carts suit DynamoDB, SQL over S3 suits Athena, and caching suits ElastiCache or DAX.

stem: A company is breaking a monolith into containerized microservices. It wants no servers or clusters of EC2 instances to manage, and requests routed to services by URL path. Which choices fit? (Choose two.)
options: Use Amazon EC2 Dedicated Hosts for each microservice
Run Docker on one large self-managed EC2 instance
Use an Application Load Balancer with path-based routing rules
Use a Network Load Balancer with path-based routing rules per service
Run the containers on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate
explanation: Fargate runs ECS tasks without EC2 instances to manage, and an ALB routes requests by path (for example /orders and /users) to separate target groups. A Network Load Balancer works at layer 4 and cannot route by URL path.

stem: A stateless web tier has a steady minimum load and unpredictable peaks. Which choices lower cost while keeping the minimum capacity reliable? (Choose two.)
options: Use Dedicated Hosts for both the base and the peaks
Run every instance On-Demand with no discounts so capacity is never at risk
Cover the steady base with a Savings Plan or Reserved Instances
Use Spot Instances in the Auto Scaling group for the peaks
Buy Reserved Instances sized for the highest peak
explanation: Commitments are cheapest for capacity that always runs, and Spot in a mixed instances Auto Scaling group covers interruptible peaks at a deep discount. Reserving for the highest peak pays for idle capacity most of the time.

stem: A company must keep scanned documents for 10 years. They are retrieved a few times a year, and when they are, a 12-hour wait is acceptable. Which storage class is cheapest?
options: S3 Glacier Deep Archive
S3 Standard-IA
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
S3 One Zone-IA
explanation: Deep Archive is the lowest-cost S3 class, with standard retrievals within 12 hours, which matches the requirement. Glacier Instant Retrieval gives millisecond access at a higher storage price.

stem: Consumers of an SQS standard queue take about 4 minutes to process each message. Some messages are being processed twice by different consumers. What is the most likely fix?
options: Raise the visibility timeout above the processing time
Lower the message retention period to one minute
Turn on long polling with a 20-second wait time
Lower the queue's delivery delay to zero seconds
explanation: If processing outlasts the visibility timeout (30 seconds by default) the message becomes visible again and another consumer picks it up. Setting the timeout above the processing time, or extending it while working, stops the duplicates. Consumers should still be idempotent, since standard queues are at-least-once.

stem: An ALB keeps sending requests to an instance whose application has crashed, although the instance itself is running. What should be changed?
options: Switch the target group protocol from HTTP to TCP
Raise the ALB's idle timeout to 4,000 seconds
Turn on EC2 detailed monitoring for the instances
Point the target group health check at an application path
explanation: A target group health check against an application URL (for example /health) detects a crashed app, so the ALB stops routing to it. With the ELB health check type on the Auto Scaling group, the instance is also replaced.

stem: A team uses a 200 GB gp2 volume only to get more IOPS, although it needs just 50 GB of space. It needs 6,000 IOPS. Which change provides this at lower cost?
options: Use a 50 GB gp3 volume provisioned with 6,000 IOPS
Use a 2 TB gp2 volume to gain baseline IOPS
Use a 50 GB st1 volume striped with RAID 0
Use a 50 GB sc1 volume with burst credits
explanation: gp3 lets IOPS and throughput be provisioned independently of size, starting at 3,000 IOPS and 125 MB/s, and costs less per GB than gp2. gp2 ties IOPS to volume size, so it forces paying for unused space.

stem: A SaaS application's relational database is idle most of the night and spikes unpredictably by day. The company wants capacity to adjust automatically in fine-grained steps without managing instance sizes. Which option fits?
options: Amazon Redshift provisioned clusters
Amazon Aurora Serverless v2
Self-managed MySQL on EC2 Spot Instances
Amazon RDS with a fixed instance size
explanation: Aurora Serverless v2 scales capacity in fine-grained increments in seconds as load changes, and can scale down very low (to zero ACUs where auto-pause is supported). A fixed instance must be sized for the peak.

stem: Employees authenticate to an on-premises Microsoft Active Directory. The company wants them to use those same credentials to sign in to the AWS Management Console of a single AWS account. Which approach fits?
options: Create matching IAM users and synchronize passwords by script each night
Give every employee the root user credentials of the account
Federate through IAM Identity Center with AD as the identity source
Configure Amazon Cognito identity pools for the console users
explanation: IAM Identity Center can use Active Directory (through AWS Directory Service or AD Connector) as its identity source, so users sign in with existing credentials and receive role-based console access. Duplicated IAM users create a second set of credentials to manage.

stem: Administrators need shell access to Linux instances in private subnets. The company wants no inbound SSH ports open and every session logged. Which solution fits?
options: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager
A Site-to-Site VPN with SSH open from the whole corporate range
EC2 key pairs shared through a central file server
A bastion host in a public subnet with port 22 open
explanation: Session Manager opens shell sessions through the SSM Agent over outbound HTTPS, with no inbound ports and with session logs to CloudWatch Logs or S3. A bastion host still needs SSH open and its own patching.

stem: An EC2 instance has an unencrypted EBS data volume. The company must encrypt it with minimal data loss risk. Which approach works?
options: Turn on S3 default encryption for the bucket that stores EBS snapshots
Select Enable encryption on the attached volume in the EC2 console
Snapshot the volume, copy the snapshot encrypted, and create a new volume
Detach the volume and attach it again with the encrypted flag set
explanation: An existing EBS volume cannot be encrypted in place. Copying a snapshot with encryption and creating a volume from it produces an encrypted copy to swap in. Turning on EBS encryption by default covers only new volumes.

stem: A company stores thumbnails that can be regenerated from originals at any time. They are accessed infrequently but need millisecond access. Which storage class is cheapest?
options: S3 Standard-IA
S3 One Zone-IA
S3 Standard
S3 Glacier Deep Archive
explanation: One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ at about 20 percent less than Standard-IA, which is acceptable for data that can be re-created if the AZ is lost. Deep Archive cannot give millisecond access.

stem: A few malformed messages keep failing and returning to an SQS queue, blocking worker capacity. The team wants them set aside for later analysis. What should be configured?
options: A dead-letter queue with a maxReceiveCount redrive policy
Message retention of 14 days on the source SQS queue
A shorter visibility timeout so failures retry more often
A FIFO queue so malformed messages are removed automatically
explanation: A redrive policy moves a message to the dead-letter queue after it has been received maxReceiveCount times without being deleted, so it stops cycling and can be inspected. Retention only controls how long unprocessed messages are kept.

stem: A company can tolerate losing at most 15 minutes of data and must be back online within 1 hour after a disaster. What do these two figures describe?
options: An SLA of 15 minutes and an MTTR of 1 hour
An RTO of 15 minutes and an RPO of 1 hour
An RPO of 1 hour and an MTBF of 15 minutes
An RPO of 15 minutes and an RTO of 1 hour
explanation: The recovery point objective is the maximum acceptable data loss, measured in time, and the recovery time objective is the maximum acceptable time to restore service.

stem: A company is moving Windows applications that use SMB file shares integrated with Microsoft Active Directory, with DFS namespaces and Windows ACLs. Which service fits?
options: Amazon FSx for Lustre Persistent
Amazon S3 with S3 Access Points
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
Amazon EFS with Standard storage
explanation: FSx for Windows File Server provides fully managed native Windows file shares over SMB with AD integration, NTFS ACLs and DFS. EFS is NFS for Linux clients.

stem: A company runs identical application stacks in us-east-1, eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1. Each user should be sent to the Region that gives them the lowest network latency. Which Route 53 policy fits?
options: Simple routing
Geolocation routing
Latency routing
Weighted routing
explanation: Latency routing answers with the Region that has the lowest measured latency for the user's resolver. Geolocation routes by the user's location, which is about compliance or localization and is not always the fastest path.

stem: A company runs Linux-based microservices on x86 EC2 instances. The code is in interpreted languages and runs on ARM without changes. How can it get better price performance?
options: Move to Dedicated Instances for isolation
Turn on EC2 detailed monitoring
Move to AWS Graviton-based instance types
Move to the largest x86 instance size
explanation: Graviton (ARM-based) instances offer up to 40 percent better price performance than comparable x86 instances for many workloads, and interpreted languages often need no code change. Larger x86 instances raise cost.

stem: An IAM user has an identity-based policy that allows s3:* on a bucket. The bucket policy explicitly denies s3:DeleteObject to that user. What happens when the user tries to delete an object?
options: The request is denied because an explicit deny always wins
The request is allowed because the identity policy allows s3:*
The request is denied only if the user signed in without MFA
The request is allowed because identity policies are evaluated first
explanation: In IAM policy evaluation an explicit deny in any applicable policy overrides every allow. Order of evaluation does not let an allow win over a deny.

stem: A static website is stored in an S3 bucket and served through Amazon CloudFront. Users must not be able to bypass CloudFront and read objects straight from the bucket. What should the architect configure?
options: A public bucket policy combined with S3 static website hosting enabled
S3 Transfer Acceleration together with a CloudFront geo restriction
A VPC gateway endpoint for S3 attached to the CloudFront distribution
Origin access control (OAC) and a bucket policy that trusts CloudFront
explanation: Origin access control signs CloudFront's requests to S3, and the bucket policy allows only that distribution, so direct requests to the bucket are refused. OAC replaces the older origin access identity.

stem: A company uses a customer managed KMS key for SSE-KMS and must rotate the key material every year without re-encrypting existing data or changing applications. What should it do?
options: Delete the key each year and let AWS create a replacement
Create a new key each year and re-encrypt every object by hand
Enable automatic key rotation on the customer managed key
Switch to SSE-C and upload a new key with each request
explanation: Automatic rotation creates new key material on a schedule while keeping the same key ID. Old material stays available to decrypt existing data, so applications change nothing. Deleting a key makes data encrypted under it unrecoverable.

stem: Several teams share one AWS account. Finance wants to see monthly cost for each team in Cost Explorer. What should be set up?
options: Turn on AWS CloudTrail data events for every service
Buy a separate Savings Plan for each of the teams
Tag resources by team and activate cost allocation tags
Create a separate VPC for each team in the same account
explanation: User-defined tags activated as cost allocation tags appear in Cost Explorer and the Cost and Usage Report, so costs can be grouped by team. VPCs do not separate billing.

stem: A ride-sharing app sends location updates from 100,000 devices every second. Several applications must read the same stream in real time, in order per device, and replay the last 24 hours if needed. Which service fits?
options: Amazon SQS standard queue
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
Amazon SNS standard topic
Amazon S3 with event notifications
explanation: Kinesis Data Streams orders records per partition key, lets multiple consumers read the same data independently, and retains it for 24 hours by default (up to 365 days) for replay. An SQS message is consumed once and then deleted.

stem: A company wants a low-cost DR plan with an RTO of a few hours. Data must be continuously replicated to a second Region, but application servers should run there only during a disaster. Which strategy is this?
options: Backup and restore only
Pilot light
Warm standby
Multi-site active/active
explanation: Pilot light keeps the core (replicated databases, AMIs, infrastructure as code) ready in the DR Region and turns on and scales the application servers only when needed. Warm standby keeps a scaled-down copy of everything running all the time.

stem: An analytics job reads millions of small objects from one S3 bucket and hits throttling (503 Slow Down) on a single key prefix. What helps most?
options: Convert the bucket to S3 One Zone-IA storage
Turn on S3 Object Lock in governance mode
Spread the objects across several key prefixes
Move every object into one larger combined prefix
explanation: S3 supports at least 3,500 writes and 5,500 reads per second per prefix, and request rates scale across prefixes, so parallel prefixes multiply throughput. Storage class does not change per-prefix request limits.

stem: A financial trading application uses TCP connections, needs to handle millions of requests per second with ultra-low latency, and requires one static IP address per AZ. Which load balancer fits?
options: Classic Load Balancer
Network Load Balancer
Gateway Load Balancer
Application Load Balancer
explanation: The NLB operates at layer 4, scales to millions of requests per second with very low latency, and supports a static or Elastic IP per AZ. The ALB is layer 7 and has no static IPs.

stem: A containerized batch platform uses Spot Instances and sees frequent interruptions in one instance type. Which approach improves Spot availability?
options: Switch the fleet to a cluster placement group for all of the instances
Use only the single cheapest instance type in one Availability Zone
Diversify across many instance types and AZs with price-capacity-optimized allocation
Set a maximum Spot price well above the On-Demand price
explanation: AWS recommends flexibility across instance types, sizes and AZs, with the price-capacity-optimized allocation strategy choosing the pools least likely to be interrupted. A single cheapest pool is the one most likely to run out.

stem: A security team wants to stop member accounts from leaving AWS Organizations or turning off AWS CloudTrail, while still letting account administrators manage everything else. What should they do?
options: Attach an SCP denying those actions to the member OUs
Remove the IAM administrator role from every member account
Attach a permissions boundary to the management account root user
Enable CloudTrail in each account and rely on CloudWatch alarms
explanation: A deny-list SCP blocks organizations:LeaveOrganization and cloudtrail:StopLogging or DeleteTrail for every principal in the targeted OUs, while other permissions keep flowing from IAM. Alarms only notify after the damage, and SCPs do not affect the management account anyway.

stem: A news site on Amazon RDS for MySQL has heavy read traffic that is slowing down writes from the editors. Which change scales reads with minimal application changes?
options: Convert the database to a larger instance class with more vCPUs
Add read replicas and send read queries to the replica endpoints
Move the database storage from General Purpose SSD to Magnetic
Enable Multi-AZ so the standby instance can answer read queries
explanation: Read replicas copy data asynchronously and serve read-only queries, taking load off the primary. A Multi-AZ DB instance's standby does not serve reads (only the Multi-AZ DB cluster option has readable standbys), and a bigger instance only scales vertically.

stem: A company is building a REST API on Amazon API Gateway for its mobile app. Only users who signed up and signed in through the app should be able to call it. Which option needs the least custom code?
options: A Lambda authorizer that checks a hardcoded password
An IAM user per customer with access keys in the app
An Amazon Cognito user pool authorizer on the API
An AWS WAF rule that allows the app's IP address
explanation: A Cognito user pool handles sign-up and sign-in and issues JWTs, and API Gateway validates them with a built-in authorizer. A mobile app has no fixed IP address, and IAM users are not meant for end customers.

stem: A company replicates encrypted data between two AWS Regions and wants to decrypt in the second Region without calling the first Region's KMS endpoint. What should it use?
options: One KMS key shared through AWS RAM
AWS KMS multi-Region keys
SSE-S3 with replica modification sync
AWS managed keys for each service
explanation: Multi-Region keys share key material and key ID across Regions, so data encrypted in one Region can be decrypted in another locally. A single-Region key is usable only in its own Region.

stem: A company keeps monthly EBS snapshots for 7 years for compliance and almost never restores them. Which change lowers snapshot storage cost?
options: Convert the volumes from gp3 to io2
Enable Fast Snapshot Restore on them
Move the snapshots to the EBS Snapshots Archive tier
Copy the snapshots to a second Region
explanation: EBS Snapshots Archive stores full snapshots at up to 75 percent lower cost for rarely accessed snapshots kept 90 days or more, with restores taking up to 72 hours. Fast Snapshot Restore adds cost.

stem: A mobile game stores player profiles in Amazon DynamoDB. Players in North America, Europe and Asia must read and write with low latency, and the data must survive a Regional outage. What should be used?
options: DynamoDB Streams to S3
On-demand backups copied daily
DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)
DynamoDB global tables
explanation: Global tables replicate a table across chosen Regions, each replica accepting reads and writes, so players use the nearest Region and the others keep working if one fails. DAX is an in-Region cache.

stem: An in-memory analytics application needs a very large amount of RAM per vCPU on a single EC2 instance. Which instance family should be chosen?
options: Compute optimized (C family)
Memory optimized (R or X family)
Burstable general purpose (T family)
Accelerated computing (G family)
explanation: R and X instances have high memory-to-vCPU ratios for in-memory databases and real-time big data analytics. G instances are GPU instances for graphics and ML inference.

stem: A company must move 50 TB of files from an on-premises NFS server to Amazon EFS over its network connection, with encryption, scheduling and integrity checks handled automatically. Which service fits?
options: AWS Transfer Family
Amazon Data Firehose
AWS Database Migration Service
AWS DataSync
explanation: DataSync moves files between on-premises storage (NFS, SMB, HDFS, object) and S3, EFS or FSx, with encryption in transit, scheduling and data verification. Transfer Family provides SFTP, FTPS and FTP endpoints for partners.

stem: A mobile app needs to let signed-in users upload photos directly to Amazon S3 without embedding AWS keys in the app. Which service provides temporary, limited AWS credentials to the app's users?
options: AWS IAM Identity Center permission sets
Amazon Cognito identity pools
AWS Directory Service Simple AD
AWS Secrets Manager with rotation
explanation: Cognito identity pools exchange a signed-in user's token for temporary AWS credentials scoped by an IAM role, so the app never holds long-term keys. IAM Identity Center is for the workforce signing in to AWS accounts, not for customers of an app.

stem: A web application's load climbs every weekday at 8 AM and drops at 6 PM, and in between it varies with traffic. Which Auto Scaling setup handles both patterns?
options: Simple scaling with a 60-minute cooldown after every scaling event
A fixed desired capacity sized for the highest load of the week
Scheduled actions for the known times plus target tracking on CPU
Manual scaling by an operator who watches the CloudWatch graphs
explanation: Scheduled actions raise capacity before the predictable morning ramp, and target tracking adjusts within the day to keep a metric such as CPU near its target. Predictive scaling could also learn the daily cycle. A fixed size wastes money off-peak.

stem: An internal API receives a few hundred requests a day at random times and currently runs on two always-on EC2 instances behind an ALB. Which change cuts cost most?
options: Move it to larger On-Demand instances
Buy Reserved Instances for both servers
Add a third instance in another AZ
Rebuild it on API Gateway and Lambda
explanation: With API Gateway and Lambda the company pays per request and per millisecond of run time, so a lightly used API costs very little and nothing while idle. Reserved Instances discount servers that still sit idle most of the day.

stem: A gaming company runs a UDP-based service in two Regions. Clients need two static IP addresses to allowlist, and traffic must shift to the healthy Region within seconds of a failure without relying on DNS caching. Which service fits?
options: Amazon CloudFront
Route 53 latency routing
Application Load Balancer
AWS Global Accelerator
explanation: Global Accelerator gives two static anycast IP addresses, supports TCP and UDP, and reroutes to healthy endpoints in seconds over the AWS network. Route 53 failover depends on clients honoring DNS TTLs, and CloudFront and ALB do not proxy arbitrary UDP traffic.

stem: A content management system on Linux EC2 instances needs shared storage that grows and shrinks automatically with no capacity planning. Which service fits?
options: Amazon FSx for Windows
Amazon EBS gp3
EC2 instance store
Amazon EFS
explanation: EFS is an elastic NFS file system that grows and shrinks as files are added and removed, and many Linux instances can mount it at once. EBS volumes have a set size and attach to one instance (Multi-Attach aside).

stem: A 5 TB on-premises Oracle database backs a 24/7 order system. It is moving to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, its stored procedures must be rewritten for PostgreSQL, and the business allows only a 10-minute outage at cutover. Which approach fits?
options: An S3 File Gateway mounted on the Oracle server for the cutover
AWS SCT for schema conversion and AWS DMS with ongoing replication
Amazon Data Firehose streaming the tables into Aurora PostgreSQL
AWS DataSync for the data files and AWS Backup for the database
explanation: The Schema Conversion Tool (or DMS Schema Conversion) converts Oracle schema and code to PostgreSQL, and DMS full load plus change data capture keeps the target in sync while the source stays live, so cutover is only the final switch. DataSync copies files, not live database changes.

stem: A production Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL instance will run unchanged around the clock for at least three years. Which option lowers its cost the most?
options: Stop the instance each night and start it each day
Use Compute Savings Plans to cover the database
Purchase an RDS Reserved Instance for three years
Change it to an Aurora Serverless v2 cluster
explanation: RDS Reserved Instances give a large discount for a one- or three-year commitment on a steady database. Compute Savings Plans do not apply to RDS. Database Savings Plans (December 2025) do, but only on a one-year term with smaller discounts than a three-year RI. A production database must keep running at night.

stem: A company must inspect and filter all traffic leaving its VPCs for the internet, including domain-based allow lists and intrusion prevention, using a managed AWS service. Which service fits?
options: AWS Shield Advanced on the NAT gateways
Security groups on every instance in the VPCs
Amazon Route 53 health checks on outbound traffic
AWS Network Firewall
explanation: AWS Network Firewall is a managed, stateful firewall for VPCs with domain filtering and Suricata-compatible intrusion prevention rules. Security groups cannot filter by domain name or inspect payloads.

stem: What is the default encryption behavior for new objects uploaded to a new Amazon S3 bucket today?
options: They are encrypted with SSE-KMS using an AWS managed key
They are encrypted with SSE-S3 automatically
They are encrypted only if the client sends a key
They are stored unencrypted until a policy is set
explanation: Since January 2023, Amazon S3 applies SSE-S3 to every new object by default at no extra cost. SSE-KMS can be chosen as the bucket default instead.

stem: A public REST API built on API Gateway and Lambda must protect its backend from traffic bursts and give each partner its own request quota. What should the architect configure?
options: A Network Load Balancer in front of API Gateway for each partner
An SQS queue in front of API Gateway to buffer the requests
A larger Lambda memory size for each function behind the API
Usage plans with API keys, plus stage throttling limits
explanation: API Gateway throttling caps steady rate and bursts, and usage plans tied to API keys set per-client throttles and quotas. More Lambda memory makes each call faster but does not limit callers.

stem: A company wants to guarantee that objects in an S3 bucket can be read only by principals in its own AWS Organization, no matter what IAM policies exist in other accounts. What should be added to the bucket policy?
options: A Deny statement with the condition aws:PrincipalOrgID not equal to the org ID
A Deny statement for any request that arrives over HTTPS connections
An Allow statement that lists the root user of the management account
An Allow statement for the principal "*" with no conditions at all
explanation: The aws:PrincipalOrgID global condition key lets one bucket policy statement deny every principal outside the organization, without listing account IDs. Allowing "*" opens the bucket, and denying HTTPS would block legitimate encrypted traffic.

stem: A company's costs vary from day to day, so fixed budget thresholds either alert too often or too late. It wants to be notified automatically when a service's spend rises unusually compared with its normal pattern. Which service fits?
options: AWS Compute Optimizer
AWS Pricing Calculator
AWS Cost Anomaly Detection
AWS Cost and Usage Report
explanation: Cost Anomaly Detection uses machine learning on past spend to learn each service's normal pattern and sends alerts on unusual increases, with root-cause details, without fixed thresholds. The Pricing Calculator estimates planned architectures, and the CUR is raw billing data.

stem: A company must keep a copy of every new object in an S3 bucket in a second Region for disaster recovery, with most objects replicated within 15 minutes backed by an SLA. What should it configure?
options: A lifecycle rule moving the objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive
Cross-Region Replication with S3 Replication Time Control
S3 Transfer Acceleration on the source bucket and the target
Same-Region Replication into a second bucket in the same Region
explanation: Cross-Region Replication copies new objects to a bucket in another Region (both buckets need versioning), and Replication Time Control adds a 15-minute replication SLA with metrics. Transfer Acceleration speeds client uploads only.

stem: A machine learning training job in one AZ reads the same small S3 objects at very high request rates and needs consistent single-digit millisecond latency. Which storage option is designed for this?
options: S3 Standard-IA with lifecycle transitions
S3 Intelligent-Tiering with archive tiers
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval storage class
S3 Express One Zone in a directory bucket
explanation: S3 Express One Zone stores data in a single AZ in directory buckets and delivers consistent single-digit millisecond access with very high request rates, which suits latency-sensitive jobs placed in the same AZ. Glacier Instant Retrieval is for rarely accessed data.

stem: A REST API on API Gateway returns product details that change once a day, and the Lambda backend is invoked for every identical request. Which change cuts latency and backend calls with the least work?
options: Move the Lambda backend into a VPC with a NAT gateway
Raise the Lambda memory to the maximum of 10,240 MB
Enable API Gateway caching for the stage with a suitable TTL
Add an SQS queue between API Gateway and the Lambda backend
explanation: API Gateway stage caching stores responses for the TTL (up to an hour), so repeated requests are served without invoking Lambda. A queue would make a synchronous API asynchronous.

stem: A Lambda function writes to a relational database. During spikes it opens thousands of connections and the database runs out of connections. Which change fixes this with the least code change?
options: Turn on Multi-AZ for the RDS database instance
Put Amazon RDS Proxy between Lambda and the database
Raise the Lambda timeout to the maximum of 15 minutes
Move the Lambda functions into a public subnet
explanation: RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections, so many concurrent Lambda invocations reuse a small number of connections. Multi-AZ adds a standby for availability but does not add connection capacity.

stem: A chatty application sends terabytes a day between application servers in one AZ and a cache cluster in another AZ in the same Region. Which design change reduces data transfer charges while keeping high availability?
options: Move the cache cluster into a different AWS Region instead
Route the traffic through a NAT gateway in each of the AZs
Read from a cache node in the same AZ as each app server
Send all of the cache traffic over the public internet instead
explanation: Data transfer between AZs is charged in each direction, while traffic within the same AZ over private IPs is free. Keeping replicas in each AZ and reading locally keeps HA and cuts cross-AZ charges. A NAT gateway adds processing charges.

stem: A company runs a high-profile website on CloudFront and an Application Load Balancer. It wants advanced DDoS protection, 24/7 access to the AWS Shield Response Team, and protection against scaling charges caused by an attack. What should it subscribe to?
options: Amazon GuardDuty Extended Threat Detection
AWS Shield Advanced
AWS Shield Standard
AWS Firewall Manager alone
explanation: Shield Advanced adds enhanced detection, the Shield Response Team and cost protection for scaling during a DDoS attack. Shield Standard is automatic and free but has none of those.

stem: A data lake uses SSE-KMS on a bucket with millions of small objects, and KMS request costs and throttling are rising. Which change reduces KMS calls without lowering security?
options: Enable S3 Bucket Keys on the bucket
Use client-side encryption with no key
Switch every object to SSE-C
Turn off default encryption
explanation: An S3 Bucket Key is a bucket-level key derived from the KMS key, which lets S3 create data keys locally and cuts KMS requests by up to 99 percent. Turning off encryption lowers security.

stem: A company is setting up a new multi-account environment and wants a prebuilt landing zone with guardrails, centralized logging and an account factory for new accounts. Which service delivers this?
options: AWS Control Tower
AWS Service Catalog AppRegistry
AWS Resource Access Manager
AWS Systems Manager Fleet Manager
explanation: Control Tower sets up a landing zone on AWS Organizations with preventive and detective controls, a log archive account, an audit account and Account Factory. Resource Access Manager only shares resources such as subnets between accounts.

stem: An Amazon EFS file system holds 20 TB, but only about 10 percent of the files are accessed in a given month. How can storage cost drop with no application change?
options: Switch the throughput mode to Provisioned with a lower setting
Enable EFS lifecycle management to move files to Infrequent Access
Copy the files to EBS gp3 volumes and attach them to each instance
Move the file system to Max I/O performance mode for lower cost
explanation: EFS lifecycle policies move files not accessed for a set period to the Infrequent Access (or Archive) storage class at a much lower price, and back on access if configured. Throughput and performance modes do not change the per-GB storage price.

stem: A company runs 200 on-premises servers and wants DR in AWS with continuous block-level replication, low-cost staging resources, and recovery in minutes with an RPO of seconds. Which service fits?
options: AWS Backup with daily plans
AWS DataSync scheduled tasks
AWS Application Migration Service
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery
explanation: Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates servers into a low-cost staging area and launches recovery instances in minutes. Application Migration Service uses similar replication but is meant for one-time migrations, and DataSync copies files rather than whole servers.

stem: A team runs short, unpredictable container workloads and wants to pay only for the vCPU and memory each task uses, with no EC2 capacity to manage. Which option fits?
options: Amazon ECS tasks on AWS Fargate
Amazon ECS on EC2 Reserved Instances
Docker on one EC2 Dedicated Host
Amazon EKS on self-managed EC2 nodes
explanation: Fargate runs containers without servers and bills per second for the vCPU and memory each task requests. Reserved Instances and Dedicated Hosts commit to capacity whether or not tasks run.

stem: A company wants to run SQL or Apache Flink applications that compute rolling one-minute metrics over a Kinesis data stream in real time. Which service fits?
options: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
Amazon Athena with federated queries
AWS Glue crawlers on a schedule
Amazon Redshift with nightly COPY loads
explanation: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink (formerly Kinesis Data Analytics) runs Flink applications on streaming data with windowed aggregations in real time. Nightly loads and crawlers are batch, not real time.

stem: A company is moving an on-premises application that uses Apache ActiveMQ with the JMS API and MQTT to AWS. It wants a managed broker without rewriting the messaging code. Which service fits?
options: Amazon MQ
Amazon SNS
Amazon SQS
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
explanation: Amazon MQ is a managed message broker for Apache ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ that supports the standard APIs and protocols (JMS, AMQP, MQTT, STOMP), so existing code keeps working. SQS and SNS would need the messaging code rewritten.

stem: A company runs fault-tolerant batch containers on ECS with Fargate and wants to cut compute cost without managing EC2 instances. Which option fits?
options: Buy EC2 Instance Savings Plans for the tasks
Raise each task's vCPU and memory allocation
Move the tasks to Dedicated Hosts in a single AZ
Run the tasks with the Fargate Spot capacity provider
explanation: Fargate Spot runs interruption-tolerant tasks on spare capacity at a steep discount, still with no instances to manage. EC2 Instance Savings Plans do not cover Fargate (Compute Savings Plans do).

stem: An application has web instances behind an internet-facing ALB and app instances behind an internal ALB. Which security group rules follow least privilege? (Choose two.)
options: Web instances allow HTTPS only from the internet-facing ALB's security group
Web instances allow SSH from 0.0.0.0/0 so that admins can reach them from anywhere
App instances allow all traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 for easier troubleshooting
Every security group allows all outbound and all inbound traffic
App instances allow traffic only from the internal ALB's security group
explanation: Referencing a security group as the source lets only members of that group connect, so each tier accepts traffic only from the tier in front of it. Open SSH and open inbound rules widen the attack surface.

stem: A company archives legal records in Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval for ten years and must be able to prove the records were never changed or deleted. Which steps meet this? (Choose two.)
options: Rely on IAM policies that deny delete actions for regular users
Store a second copy in S3 One Zone-IA for faster restores
Enable S3 Versioning, which Object Lock requires on the bucket
Apply S3 Object Lock retention in compliance mode to the objects
Turn on S3 Intelligent-Tiering archive access tiers instead
explanation: S3 Object Lock works only on versioned buckets, and compliance mode retention stops anyone from deleting or overwriting the locked versions, whatever their storage class. IAM policies can be changed by administrators, so they do not prove immutability.

stem: A CloudTrail review shows a CI server on premises calls AWS APIs with access keys created three years ago for a developer's IAM user. Which actions improve security? (Choose two.)
options: Use IAM Roles Anywhere so the server gets temporary credentials
Deactivate and delete the old access keys once the server is moved
Attach the developer's keys to a second IAM user as a backup
Email the keys to the security team so they have a copy on file
Raise the session duration of the developer's console sessions
explanation: IAM Roles Anywhere lets workloads outside AWS use X.509 certificates to obtain temporary credentials for an IAM role, which removes long-term keys from the server. After switching, the old keys should be deactivated and deleted. Copying or emailing keys spreads the exposure.

stem: Which features make an Amazon Aurora cluster resilient within one Region? (Choose two.)
options: Aurora Replicas in other AZs promoted on failure
A single DB instance with all of its storage kept in one AZ
Instance store volumes holding the data files
Six copies of data stored across three AZs
Manual snapshots taken once a week by hand
explanation: Aurora storage keeps six copies across three AZs and heals itself, and if the writer fails an Aurora Replica in another AZ is promoted, usually in under a minute. Weekly manual snapshots would lose up to a week of data.

stem: A data pipeline downloads multi-GB objects from Amazon S3 and is limited by single-stream download speed. Which actions improve throughput? (Choose two.)
options: Enable MFA Delete on the source bucket
Move the objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive for faster reads
Run more parallel connections from the client
Turn on S3 Versioning on the source bucket
Use byte-range fetches to download parts in parallel
explanation: Byte-range GETs split one object into ranges fetched in parallel, and more parallel connections add aggregate throughput. Versioning and MFA Delete are data protection features, and Deep Archive needs hours to restore.

stem: A dynamic web application in one Region serves users worldwide. Which steps improve their experience without deploying to more Regions? (Choose two.)
options: Turn off TLS so pages load with fewer round trips
Move the database into a public subnet for faster access
Put CloudFront in front of the ALB to cache static content
Use CloudFront for dynamic content over the AWS backbone
Replace the ALB with a single larger EC2 instance
