explanation: CloudFront caches static assets at the edge and also accelerates dynamic, uncached requests by ending TLS near the user and using persistent connections over the AWS network to the origin. A public database and no TLS are security failures.

stem: Which design choices make a multi-tier application more loosely coupled? (Choose two.)
options: Hardcode the private IP address of each downstream server
Have each tier call the next one synchronously and wait
Communicate between tiers through queues or event buses
Put a load balancer in front of each tier's instances
Store all shared state in local files on one instance
explanation: Queues and event buses let producers and consumers work independently, and load balancers hide individual instances behind one endpoint so instances can come and go. Hardcoded IPs and shared local files tie components to specific servers.

stem: An S3 bucket has grown to 500 TB, with many old object versions and abandoned incomplete multipart uploads. Which lifecycle rules cut cost? (Choose two.)
options: Turn on S3 Object Lock in compliance mode for every object in the bucket
Abort incomplete multipart uploads after a few days
Turn on Cross-Region Replication to a second bucket
Turn on S3 Transfer Acceleration for the whole bucket
Expire noncurrent object versions after a set number of days
explanation: Noncurrent versions and incomplete multipart upload parts are billed as storage, and lifecycle rules can expire versions and abort stale uploads automatically. Replication doubles storage, and Object Lock prevents deletion.

stem: What does scaling out mean for a web tier on Amazon EC2?
options: Raising the IOPS of the instance's EBS volume
Adding more instances behind the load balancer
Changing to an instance type with more memory
Moving the instance into a different AZ
explanation: Scaling out (horizontal scaling) adds instances, which pairs with load balancing and Auto Scaling. Changing to a bigger instance type is scaling up, which has a hard ceiling and usually means downtime.

stem: Why does AWS recommend deploying across multiple Availability Zones?
options: AZs are physically separate, so one AZ's failure leaves the others running
Instances in more than one AZ always receive a lower hourly price
AZs are in different countries, which satisfies every data residency rule
Multiple AZs remove the need to take backups of the application data
explanation: Each AZ has independent power, cooling and networking and sits a meaningful distance from the others within the Region, so failures stay contained. All AZs of a Region are in the same geographic area.

stem: Which storage service presents block-level volumes that attach to a single EC2 instance like a hard drive?
options: Amazon S3
Amazon EBS
Amazon EFS
Amazon FSx for Lustre
explanation: EBS provides block storage volumes for EC2. EFS and FSx are file systems shared over the network, and S3 is object storage accessed through an API.

stem: An application needs single-digit millisecond key-value lookups at any scale, with a flexible schema and no servers to manage. Which database fits?
options: Amazon Redshift
Amazon DynamoDB
Amazon RDS for MySQL
Amazon Neptune
explanation: DynamoDB is a serverless key-value and document database with consistent single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. Redshift is for analytics, Neptune for graphs.

stem: A team of 25 analysts all need the same read-only access to Amazon Athena and Amazon S3. What is the simplest way to manage their permissions?
options: Attach the policy to the root user so that every analyst inherits it
Give all of the analysts one shared IAM user and one shared password
Put the analysts in an IAM group and attach the policy to the group
Attach the same inline policy to each of the 25 analysts one by one
explanation: Policies attached to an IAM group apply to every member, so adding or removing an analyst is a single change. (With IAM Identity Center the same idea is a permission set assigned to a group.) Inline policies on each user drift apart over time.

stem: A security group allows inbound HTTPS from anywhere, and all of its outbound rules have been removed. Can the instance still send responses to those HTTPS clients?
options: No, unless the subnet's network ACL also allows HTTPS outbound
No, every response packet needs a matching outbound rule on port 443
Yes, security groups are stateful and allow return traffic automatically
Yes, because AWS Shield Standard automatically allows the responses
explanation: Security groups track connections, so replies to allowed inbound traffic are allowed out regardless of outbound rules. Network ACLs are the stateless layer that needs ephemeral port rules.

stem: Which option lets the customer supply and manage its own key with every S3 request, while S3 performs the encryption?
options: DSSE-KMS
SSE-S3
SSE-KMS
SSE-C
explanation: With SSE-C the client sends the key in each request; S3 encrypts or decrypts and then discards the key. SSE-S3 and SSE-KMS keys are managed by AWS services.

stem: Which EC2 purchase option has no commitment, bills per second for Linux, and suits short-term, unpredictable workloads that cannot be interrupted?
options: Standard Reserved Instances
Savings Plans
Spot Instances
On-Demand Instances
explanation: On-Demand needs no commitment and cannot be reclaimed by AWS. Spot is cheaper but can be interrupted, and Reserved Instances and Savings Plans need a one- or three-year commitment.

stem: Consumers poll an SQS queue in a tight loop and most receives come back empty, adding cost. Which setting reduces empty responses?
options: Switch the standard queue to a FIFO queue
Enable long polling with a 20-second wait
Set the message retention period to 60 seconds
Lower the visibility timeout to zero seconds
explanation: Long polling makes a receive request wait up to 20 seconds for a message to arrive, which cuts empty responses and request charges. Visibility timeout and retention do not affect empty receives.

stem: Which DR strategy has the lowest cost and the longest recovery time?
options: Multi-site active/active
Backup and restore
Pilot light
Warm standby
explanation: Backup and restore keeps only backups in the DR location and rebuilds everything after a disaster, so it costs least but takes hours or more. Active/active costs most and recovers almost instantly.

stem: A company trains deep learning models and needs instances with powerful NVIDIA GPUs. Which family fits?
options: Burstable general purpose (T family)
Compute optimized (C family)
Accelerated computing (P family)
Memory optimized (R family)
explanation: P instances carry high-end GPUs for machine learning training and HPC. C instances are CPU-only.

stem: A company runs a self-managed MongoDB database of JSON product documents on EC2. It wants a managed AWS database that works with its existing MongoDB drivers and queries. Which purpose-built database fits?
options: Amazon Neptune
Amazon Redshift
Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra)
explanation: DocumentDB is a managed document database that supports the MongoDB API, so existing drivers and most queries work with little change. Neptune is a graph database, Keyspaces is Cassandra-compatible, and Redshift is a data warehouse.

stem: An application calls AssumeRole and receives credentials for an IAM role. Which statement about those credentials is true?
options: They work only in the AWS Management Console sign-in
They are the role's long-term access keys sent by email
They are temporary, include a session token, and expire
They never expire until the role is deleted from IAM
explanation: AWS STS returns an access key ID, a secret access key and a session token that expire after the session duration (15 minutes up to the role's maximum, 1 hour by default). Roles have no long-term access keys of their own.

stem: Instances in a private subnet have only IPv6 addresses. They must start connections to internet update servers, but nothing on the internet may start a connection to them. What should the route table point at?
options: A virtual private gateway on the VPC
An egress-only internet gateway
A gateway VPC endpoint for the update servers
An internet gateway with public IPv6 routing
explanation: An egress-only internet gateway is the IPv6 counterpart of NAT for this purpose: it allows outbound IPv6 connections and their replies but blocks connections started from the internet. IPv6 addresses are globally routable, so a plain internet gateway route would allow inbound connections. Gateway endpoints exist only for S3 and DynamoDB.

stem: An application in Account B must decrypt data encrypted with a customer managed KMS key in Account A. What must be configured?
options: The key policy in A allows Account B, and an IAM policy in B allows kms:Decrypt
Only an IAM policy in Account B that allows kms:Decrypt on the key's ARN
Only a bucket policy in Account A that allows Account B to read the objects
Nothing, because KMS keys are shared across all accounts by default
explanation: Cross-account use of a KMS key needs both sides: the key policy must trust the other account, and that account must grant its principals permission. An IAM policy alone cannot reach a key the key policy does not open.

stem: Objects are moved to S3 Standard-IA and then deleted after 10 days. What happens to the charges?
options: Deleting objects in Standard-IA within 30 days is blocked
They are billed for 10 days with no other charge at all
They are billed for the 30-day minimum storage duration
They are billed for the 90-day Glacier minimum duration
explanation: Standard-IA and One Zone-IA have a 30-day minimum storage charge, so short-lived objects cost more there than in Standard. Glacier Instant and Flexible Retrieval have 90-day minimums and Deep Archive 180.

stem: An application must hold every new message in an SQS queue for 5 minutes before any consumer can see it. Which feature does this?
options: A visibility timeout of 5 minutes on the queue
A delay queue with a 5-minute delivery delay
A message retention period of 5 minutes
A dead-letter queue that redrives after 5 minutes
explanation: Delivery delay (up to 15 minutes) hides new messages from consumers for the set time. Visibility timeout only applies after a consumer has received a message.

stem: An Auto Scaling group behind an ALB uses only EC2 status checks. Instances with a hung web server are never replaced. What fixes this?
options: Turn on termination protection for each instance
Turn on ELB health checks for the group
Lower the group's maximum size to the desired size
Raise the default cooldown to 15 minutes
explanation: With ELB health checks enabled, the Auto Scaling group treats an instance the load balancer reports unhealthy as unhealthy and replaces it. EC2 status checks only see instance and host problems.

stem: A NoSQL database on EC2 needs very high random I/O on locally attached NVMe SSD storage and replicates its own data. Which instance family fits?
options: Burstable performance (T family)
Storage optimized (I family)
Compute optimized (C family)
Accelerated computing (G family)
explanation: I family instances have large, fast local NVMe instance storage for I/O-heavy databases that handle their own replication. The data is ephemeral, which is why the database must replicate.

stem: A team needs full-text search and dashboards over application logs with near real-time indexing. Which service fits?
options: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
Amazon OpenSearch Service
Amazon ElastiCache
Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
explanation: OpenSearch Service indexes documents for full-text search and log analytics and includes OpenSearch Dashboards. Glacier is archival storage with retrieval delays.

stem: A company wants administrators to be able to terminate EC2 instances only when they signed in with MFA. How can this be enforced in IAM?
options: Turn on MFA for the root user and leave the IAM policies as they are
Add an aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent condition to the policy statement
Use an SCP that allows ec2:TerminateInstances for the whole account
Require HTTPS for the AWS Management Console sign-in page
explanation: The aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent condition key lets a policy allow, or deny, an action depending on whether the session was authenticated with MFA. MFA on the root user does nothing for other identities.

stem: A company stores thousands of files in Amazon S3 and must find which objects contain personally identifiable information such as names and credit card numbers. Which service does this?
options: Amazon Detective
Amazon Macie
AWS Config
Amazon Inspector
explanation: Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover sensitive data in S3 and report it. Inspector looks for software vulnerabilities, and Config records resource configurations.

stem: A company wants every new EBS volume and snapshot in a Region to be encrypted automatically, even if a user forgets to select encryption. What should it enable?
options: S3 default encryption on the bucket used for snapshots
EBS encryption by default for that Region
An AWS Config rule that deletes unencrypted volumes
Automatic rotation on the AWS managed key for EBS
explanation: EBS encryption by default is an account-level, per-Region setting that forces encryption on new volumes and snapshot copies. A Config rule would only detect and react afterward.

stem: An SNS topic publishes all order events. One subscribed SQS queue should receive only events where the order region is EU. What is the simplest way to do this?
options: Use an SQS FIFO queue with region as the message group
Create a separate SNS topic for each order region
Have the consumer delete the non-EU messages it receives
Add a subscription filter policy on the region attribute
explanation: SNS subscription filter policies match message attributes (or the message body) so each subscriber receives only the messages it wants. Filtering in the consumer wastes delivery and processing.

stem: A small cluster of critical instances must not share underlying hardware, so a single rack failure affects at most one of them. Which placement option fits?
options: A cluster placement group
A Dedicated Host for the cluster
A spread placement group
An On-Demand Capacity Reservation
explanation: A spread placement group puts each instance on distinct racks with separate power and network (up to seven running instances per AZ per group). A cluster group does the opposite, packing instances close for low latency.

stem: A company is moving a NetApp storage array used by both Linux (NFS) and Windows (SMB) clients and depends on its snapshots and replication. Which service keeps those features?
options: AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway
Amazon EFS Standard
Amazon FSx for OpenZFS
Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
explanation: FSx for NetApp ONTAP runs ONTAP as a managed service with NFS, SMB and iSCSI access, snapshots, SnapMirror replication and data deduplication. EFS supports NFS only.

stem: A team wants to view the last 12 months of costs by service and forecast the next three months in a graphical tool. Which service fits?
options: AWS Pricing Calculator
Amazon CloudWatch
AWS Trusted Advisor
AWS Cost Explorer
explanation: Cost Explorer shows historical cost and usage, filters by service, account or tag, and forecasts future spend. The Pricing Calculator estimates new architectures, not past spend.

stem: A data team runs large Apache Spark and Hadoop jobs and needs control over the cluster's frameworks and configuration. Which service fits?
options: Amazon EMR
Amazon Athena
AWS Glue DataBrew
AWS Lambda
explanation: EMR runs managed clusters (on EC2, EKS or serverless) for Spark, Hadoop, Hive and Presto with control over frameworks and tuning. Athena is serverless SQL, not a framework platform.

stem: An SCP attached to an OU allows only Amazon S3 and Amazon EC2 actions. An IAM user in an account in that OU has the AdministratorAccess policy. What can the user do?
options: Only actions in Regions named in the SCP's Region condition key
Only S3 and EC2 actions, because the SCP limits the maximum permissions
Nothing at all, because SCPs never grant permissions on their own
Every action in the account, because AdministratorAccess grants all
explanation: Effective permissions are the intersection of the SCP and the IAM policy. The SCP does not grant anything, but it filters the administrator's allow down to S3 and EC2.

stem: A SaaS provider wants hundreds of customer VPCs to reach its service privately, without VPC peering, overlapping CIDR conflicts, or traffic crossing the internet. What should the provider build?
options: A VPC peering connection with every customer VPC across all accounts
A public Application Load Balancer protected by customer IP allow lists
A transit gateway that every one of the customers attaches their VPC to
An endpoint service behind a Network Load Balancer, shared via PrivateLink
explanation: AWS PrivateLink lets consumers create interface endpoints to a provider's endpoint service fronted by an NLB. Traffic stays on the AWS network and CIDR overlap does not matter. Peering at that scale fails on overlapping ranges.

stem: A government workload requires two independent layers of server-side encryption on objects stored in Amazon S3. Which option provides this?
options: S3 Bucket Keys
SSE-C
SSE-S3
DSSE-KMS
explanation: Dual-layer server-side encryption with KMS keys (DSSE-KMS) applies two layers of encryption to each object to meet requirements such as CNSSP 15. Bucket Keys reduce KMS calls but add no layer.

stem: A Lambda function that calls a fragile third-party API must never run more than 50 copies at once, even under heavy load. What should be configured?
options: Reserved concurrency of 50 on the function
A memory setting of 50 MB for the function
Provisioned concurrency of 50 on the function
A timeout of 50 seconds for each invocation
explanation: Reserved concurrency both guarantees and caps the number of concurrent executions of a function. Provisioned concurrency keeps environments warm to cut cold starts but is not a cap on its own.

stem: A company wants an RDS for MySQL deployment with automatic failover that is typically faster than a Multi-AZ DB instance and with standbys that can serve read traffic. Which option fits?
options: A Single-AZ DB instance with automated backups
A Multi-AZ DB instance with one standby replica
A Multi-AZ DB cluster with two readable standbys
A cross-Region read replica in a second Region
explanation: A Multi-AZ DB cluster has a writer and two readable standby instances in three AZs, with faster typical failover. The standby of a Multi-AZ DB instance takes no read traffic.

stem: An on-premises backup application writes to a physical tape library. The company wants to stop handling tapes and store backups in AWS, archived to low-cost storage, without changing its backup software. Which service fits?
options: AWS DataSync agent on a scheduled task
AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway
Amazon EFS mounted over a VPN
AWS Transfer Family with SFTP access
explanation: Tape Gateway presents a virtual tape library over iSCSI that existing backup software already understands, stores virtual tapes in S3 and archives them to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval or Deep Archive. DataSync and Transfer Family move files, not tapes the backup software can write to.

stem: Business partners must keep sending files over SFTP after the company moves its storage to Amazon S3, without changing their client setup. Which service fits?
options: Amazon AppFlow
AWS DataSync
AWS Transfer Family
S3 Transfer Acceleration
explanation: Transfer Family provides managed SFTP, FTPS, FTP and AS2 endpoints that store files directly in S3 or EFS, so partners keep their clients. DataSync is for the company's own bulk moves.

stem: A DynamoDB table stores years of order history that is rarely read, and storage, not throughput, is now most of its cost. Which change lowers it?
options: Switch the table to provisioned capacity mode
Turn on global tables in a second Region
Use the Standard-IA table class
Add a DAX cluster in front of the table
explanation: The DynamoDB Standard-Infrequent Access table class cuts storage price by about 60 percent for tables where storage dominates, at a somewhat higher per-request price. DAX and global tables add cost.

stem: Users upload large video files that are transcoded later. The web servers struggle to proxy the uploads. Which design takes the uploads off the web tier?
options: Send the video bytes through an SQS queue to the transcoders
Have clients upload straight to S3 with presigned URLs
Raise the web servers' EBS volume size for temporary files
Use sticky sessions so each upload stays on one server
explanation: Presigned URLs let clients upload directly to S3 with time-limited permission, so the web tier only issues the URL. An S3 event can then start transcoding. SQS messages are far too small for video files.

stem: Route 53 is configured with multivalue answer routing for four web servers, each with a health check. What does Route 53 return to clients?
options: Only the record for the primary server
Up to eight healthy records
Only the record with the lowest latency
All records, healthy or not, in fixed order
explanation: Multivalue answer routing returns up to eight healthy records for each query, which gives simple client-side load spreading with health checking. It is not a substitute for a load balancer.

stem: A gp3 volume delivers its IOPS but the application needs more than the 125 MB/s it currently gets. What can the architect do?
options: Switch to an sc1 Cold HDD volume of the same size
Take a snapshot of the volume every hour
Provision higher throughput on the gp3 volume
Enable encryption on the volume
explanation: gp3 throughput can be raised independently of size and IOPS, well above the 125 MB/s baseline. sc1 is a cold HDD type with lower performance.

stem: A third-party monitoring company needs to assume a role in a customer's account. How can the customer prevent the confused deputy problem?
options: Turn on S3 Block Public Access for the entire account
Share the root user password with the third-party vendor
Allow the principal "*" in the trust policy of the role
Require a unique external ID in the role's trust policy
explanation: An external ID condition in the trust policy ensures the vendor assumes the role only on behalf of the right customer, which blocks the confused deputy problem. Trusting "*" would let any AWS account try to assume the role.

stem: A company needs free, auto-renewing public TLS certificates for its Application Load Balancer and CloudFront distribution. Which service provides them?
options: AWS CloudHSM
AWS Secrets Manager
AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)
AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)
explanation: ACM issues public certificates at no charge and renews them automatically when they are used with integrated services such as ELB and CloudFront. For CloudFront the certificate must be requested in us-east-1.

stem: A company wants its AWS Backup recovery points to be immutable so that even an administrator cannot delete them before their retention ends. What should it use?
options: A lifecycle rule that moves backups to cold storage
AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode
Cross-Region copy of the backups to a second vault
An IAM policy that denies backup:DeleteRecoveryPoint
explanation: Vault Lock in compliance mode makes recovery points write once, read many: after the grace period no one, including the root user, can change the lock or delete backups early. An IAM deny can be removed by an administrator.

stem: A company is building a data lake on S3 and wants to manage fine-grained table-, column- and row-level permissions for Athena and Redshift Spectrum users in one place. Which service fits?
options: AWS Config
Amazon Cognito user pools
Amazon Macie
AWS Lake Formation
explanation: Lake Formation sets up the data lake and centrally governs fine-grained access on Glue Data Catalog tables for integrated analytics services. Macie finds sensitive data but does not grant access.

stem: A research institute shares a large public dataset in S3 and wants the people who download it to pay the request and data transfer charges. What should it enable?
options: S3 Intelligent-Tiering
Requester Pays on the bucket
Cross-Region Replication
S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoint
explanation: With Requester Pays the requester, who must be an authenticated AWS user, pays for requests and data downloaded, while the owner pays for storage.

stem: A team runs containers on Amazon ECS on EC2 and wants the cluster's EC2 capacity to grow and shrink automatically as tasks are added or removed. What should it use?
options: AWS Batch compute environments in place of the ECS service tasks
An ECS capacity provider with managed scaling on an Auto Scaling group
A fixed-size Auto Scaling group with enough capacity for the peak hour
A scheduled Lambda function that resizes the cluster once an hour
explanation: Capacity providers with managed scaling adjust the Auto Scaling group based on the capacity that tasks need. Alternatively, Fargate removes the instances altogether.

stem: A developer accidentally deleted items from a DynamoDB table 2 hours ago. Which feature, if enabled beforehand, allows restoring the table to a moment before the deletion?
options: Auto scaling of read capacity
Point-in-time recovery (PITR)
DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)
Time to Live (TTL) on items
explanation: PITR keeps continuous backups and restores the table to any second in the retention window (up to 35 days) into a new table. TTL deletes items on purpose, it does not protect them.

stem: New instances in an Auto Scaling group need several minutes to load data before they can serve traffic, and scale-out is too slow during spikes. Which feature reduces the delay?
options: Spot Instances in the launch template
A larger maximum size on the group
Shorter health check grace periods on the group
A warm pool of pre-initialized instances
explanation: A warm pool keeps pre-initialized instances stopped or running, so they join the group much faster when it scales out. Raising the maximum size does not speed up each launch.

stem: A networking account owns a VPC. Application accounts in the same organization must launch instances into its subnets. Which service shares the subnets?
options: AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM)
VPC peering between every pair of accounts
AWS Organizations tag policies
AWS Direct Connect gateway
explanation: AWS RAM shares subnets from a VPC owner to participant accounts (VPC sharing), so they launch into a centrally managed network. Peering connects separate VPCs instead of sharing one.

stem: A custom network ACL on a public subnet allows inbound HTTPS. Clients can connect but receive no responses. What is the most likely cause?
options: The instances lack an IAM role that allows inbound traffic
The security group has no outbound rule for HTTPS port 443
The internet gateway is attached to the wrong route table
The NACL has no outbound rule for ephemeral ports 1024 to 65535
explanation: Network ACLs are stateless, so return traffic to clients' ephemeral ports must be allowed outbound explicitly. Security groups would allow the return traffic automatically.

stem: A company wants to automatically tag S3 objects that contain sensitive data so different encryption and access controls can be applied. Which approach fits best?
options: Enable Amazon GuardDuty S3 Protection on the account
Turn on S3 server access logs and read them manually
Run Amazon Macie discovery jobs and act on the findings
Use AWS Trusted Advisor checks on each S3 bucket
explanation: Macie identifies sensitive data such as PII and financial data in S3 and emits findings to EventBridge, where automation can tag or move objects. GuardDuty S3 Protection detects suspicious access, not data content.

stem: Two VPCs in the same Region, owned by different teams with non-overlapping CIDRs, need private connectivity between each other only. What is the simplest option?
options: A VPC peering connection
AWS Transit Gateway with VPN
Two Site-to-Site VPN tunnels
AWS Direct Connect gateway
explanation: VPC peering connects two VPCs privately with no extra gateway to run. Transit Gateway pays off with many VPCs, and VPN and Direct Connect are for on-premises links.

stem: A company wants clickstream data captured and loaded into Amazon S3 in near real time, batched and compressed, with no consumer code to write or servers to run. Which service fits?
options: AWS Glue crawlers
Amazon Data Firehose
Amazon SQS FIFO queue
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams alone
explanation: Amazon Data Firehose (formerly Kinesis Data Firehose) buffers, optionally transforms and compresses, and delivers streaming data to S3, Redshift, OpenSearch and other destinations, fully managed. Kinesis Data Streams needs consumer code to land data in S3.

stem: A trading platform must keep running with near-zero downtime and near-zero data loss even if an entire Region fails, and cost is a lower priority. Which DR approach fits?
options: Multi-site active/active across Regions
Pilot light in a second Region
Warm standby with hourly replication
Backup and restore from daily snapshots
explanation: Multi-site active/active runs full production in more than one Region with traffic going to all of them, so losing one Region does not interrupt service. It is the most expensive strategy.

stem: A research team submits thousands of container-based batch jobs with dependencies and wants AWS to provision and scale the right compute, including Spot, automatically. Which service fits?
options: Amazon EventBridge
Amazon Lightsail
AWS Lambda
AWS Batch
explanation: AWS Batch queues jobs, handles dependencies, and provisions EC2, Spot or Fargate capacity for them. Lambda functions are limited to 15 minutes per invocation.

stem: A company with 15 AWS accounts wants one bill and to share volume pricing tiers and Savings Plan discounts across accounts. What should it use?
options: AWS Cost and Usage Report in each account
AWS Budgets in the largest account only
A separate payment card for each account
Consolidated billing in AWS Organizations
explanation: Consolidated billing combines usage across the organization's accounts, which reaches volume discount tiers sooner and lets Reserved Instance and Savings Plan discounts apply across accounts (sharing can be turned off).

stem: A company uses SCPs to limit what its own principals can do. It also wants an organization-wide ceiling on what any principal, including ones from outside the organization, can do to its S3 buckets and KMS keys. Which policy type adds this?
options: Session policies passed in each AssumeRole call
IAM permissions boundaries on the account root users
Resource control policies (RCPs) in AWS Organizations
Tag policies applied to every organizational unit
explanation: RCPs, added to AWS Organizations in late 2024, set the maximum permissions on resources in member accounts for any requester, which complements SCPs (which only limit the organization's own principals). Tag policies only standardize tags.

stem: GuardDuty reports that an EC2 instance is talking to a known command-and-control server. The security team wants to investigate the root cause with linked visualizations of the instance's network flows, API calls and related findings over time, without building its own log pipeline. Which service fits?
options: AWS Audit Manager
AWS Security Hub
Amazon Detective
Amazon Macie
explanation: Detective automatically builds a behavior graph from CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, GuardDuty findings and other sources so analysts can trace what an entity did before and after a finding. Security Hub aggregates and prioritizes findings but is not an investigation tool, and Audit Manager collects compliance evidence.

stem: A KMS key encrypts data for several tenants. The company wants decryption to fail unless the caller supplies the same tenant ID used at encryption, and wants that ID logged in CloudTrail. What should it use?
options: An encryption context containing the tenant ID
A tag on the KMS key that names each tenant
Client-side encryption with a shared static key
A separate AWS account for every tenant
explanation: An encryption context is additional authenticated data: decryption succeeds only with the exact same context, and the context appears in CloudTrail logs. Key policies can also require specific context values.

stem: A company runs a Redshift data warehouse for BI and wants to query cold historical data kept in S3 together with warehouse tables, without loading it. Which feature fits?
options: Redshift concurrency scaling
Amazon ElastiCache for Redshift
Redshift elastic resize
Amazon Redshift Spectrum
explanation: Redshift Spectrum queries data in S3 through external tables and joins it with local tables, so cold data stays in cheap storage. Concurrency scaling adds capacity for bursts of queries but does not read S3 data.

stem: Consumers of an SQS standard queue occasionally receive the same message twice. The business cannot charge a customer twice. What should the architect do?
options: Turn off retries in the SQS queue settings for the consumer group
Make processing idempotent, such as by tracking processed message IDs
Raise the queue's message retention period to the maximum of 14 days
Use short polling so that each receive call checks every server
explanation: Standard queues deliver at least once, so consumers must handle duplicates. Recording processed IDs (for example with a DynamoDB conditional write) makes a repeat harmless. Moving to FIFO is the other option, but retention and polling settings do not stop duplicates.

stem: An application in three AZs needs 6 instances to serve peak load. To stay at full capacity if one AZ fails, without waiting for new instances to launch, how many instances should run in total?
options: 9, three in each AZ
7, with one spare
12, four in each AZ
6, two in each AZ
explanation: If one AZ fails, the remaining two AZs must hold the 6 needed instances, so each AZ needs 3, which is 9 in total. Six would leave only 4 after an AZ loss, and 12 overprovisions.

stem: A clustered application on two EC2 instances in the same AZ must write to the same block volume at the same time and manages write ordering itself. Which option fits?
options: A gp3 volume attached to each instance
An instance store volume shared by both
An io2 volume with Multi-Attach enabled
An st1 volume with Multi-Attach enabled
explanation: Multi-Attach is supported on Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1 and io2) volumes in the same AZ, for applications that manage concurrent writes, such as clustered file systems. It is not available on gp3 or HDD volumes.

stem: A stateless web application runs on On-Demand x86 instances sized for peak around the clock. Which steps reduce cost? (Choose two.)
options: Move to Graviton instances after testing
Move every instance to a Dedicated Host
Buy three-year Reserved Instances sized for the peak load
Use Auto Scaling so capacity follows demand
Add a second fleet in another Region
explanation: Auto Scaling removes capacity that peak sizing leaves idle off-peak, and Graviton instances typically give better price performance. Reserving for the peak locks in the waste, and Dedicated Hosts cost more.

stem: Which practices does AWS recommend for the root user of a member account? (Choose two.)
options: Create access keys for it so scripts can call AWS APIs during outages
Share its credentials with the team so access is never lost
Use it for daily administration so that actions are never blocked
Use it only for the few tasks that require root user credentials
Protect it with MFA, or centrally manage root access through Organizations
explanation: AWS recommends limiting the root user to tasks that require it and protecting it with MFA. With centralized root access in Organizations, member accounts can even run without root credentials. Root access keys and daily use of root are both discouraged.

stem: A public web application on EC2 behind an ALB must be protected from common web exploits and must hide the instances from direct internet access. Which steps help? (Choose two.)
options: Attach an AWS WAF web ACL with managed rules to the ALB
Give each instance an Elastic IP so traffic avoids the ALB
Open the instances' security groups to 0.0.0.0/0 on all ports
Put the EC2 instances in private subnets behind the ALB
Disable TLS on the ALB to speed up WAF inspection of requests
explanation: Instances in private subnets accept traffic only through the ALB, and WAF on the ALB blocks common exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting. Elastic IPs and open security groups expose the instances directly.

stem: Which actions protect data in transit between clients and an application behind an Application Load Balancer? (Choose two.)
options: Enable EBS encryption on all of the instances that sit behind the ALB
Rotate the KMS keys that protect the RDS database
Use an HTTPS listener on the ALB with a certificate from ACM
Redirect HTTP requests on port 80 to HTTPS on port 443
Turn on S3 default encryption for the application logs
explanation: An HTTPS listener encrypts traffic between clients and the ALB, and an HTTP to HTTPS redirect makes sure no client stays on plain HTTP. EBS, S3 and RDS encryption protect data at rest.

stem: A company needs to collect streaming events in real time, store them durably in S3 in batches, and query them with SQL. Which services fit together? (Choose two.)
options: AWS Snowball Edge to move each daily batch
Amazon Data Firehose to deliver the stream to S3
Amazon ElastiCache to archive the raw events
Amazon Neptune to store the event batches
Amazon Athena to query the data in S3
explanation: Firehose captures streaming data and delivers it to S3 in batches, optionally converting it to Parquet, and Athena queries it in place with SQL. ElastiCache is an in-memory cache, not durable archival storage.

stem: A startup wants a REST API that scales from zero to thousands of requests per second with no servers to patch and pay-per-request pricing. Which services fit? (Choose two.)
options: AWS Elastic Beanstalk on EC2
Amazon API Gateway
Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances
An Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance
AWS Lambda
explanation: API Gateway and Lambda are both fully managed, scale automatically and bill per request and duration. EC2 instances, Beanstalk environments on EC2 and provisioned RDS instances run and bill even when idle.

stem: Which components together give a web tier automatic recovery from instance and AZ failures? (Choose two.)
options: An Auto Scaling group spanning several AZs
A cluster placement group in a single Availability Zone
Instance store volumes for the web content
A single EC2 instance with an Elastic IP
An Elastic Load Balancer with health checks
explanation: The load balancer stops sending traffic to failed targets, and the multi-AZ Auto Scaling group replaces them and rebalances across AZs. A single instance or a single-AZ cluster group remains a single point of failure.

stem: Which workloads are good fits for AWS Lambda? (Choose two.)
options: A video render that runs for three hours per job
Processing each new S3 object in a few seconds
Running short API handlers that scale with requests
A database server that must keep running nonstop
A licensed application that is tied to one physical server
explanation: Lambda suits event-driven, short-lived work: it runs up to 15 minutes per invocation and scales with events. Long renders, always-on databases and host-bound licenses fit EC2 or containers instead.
